findings: Only sample deadline storage/type and the Web-only weapon_motion scheduling clock change; reversing those changes plus comment restores full original file bytes.
Monotonic microseconds match real_usec used by the unchanged consumer; only actual current frame snapshots are emitted, with no synthetic catch-up samples or backdated timestamps.
Original occupied/FX/apex eligibility, _record payload, event append/print, elapsed, physics, state, controls, pause early return and other event sampling remain byte-identical.
GDScript and short-circuits OS.has_feature(web) before Time.get_ticks_usec; non-Web path does not query the new scheduling clock.
Deadline is set from now, so 100ms is a minimum sampling interval while frames and eligibility permit, not a guaranteed real-time frequency. Paused/stalled frames are not fabricated.
limitations: No proof that sparse sampling caused the earlier false result; evaluation prefix was not captured.
No live pass, native pass, full original three-consumer pass, public delivery, performance guarantee, physical-device or full UI acceptance.
Higher Web event rate during slow time may increase console/serialization overhead; original live consumers remain required.
Foundry basis membership is separately owned by CI reviewer; this report does not assert a rebuild decision.
